newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish bank shares jump in merger/results spree.
newsitem.headline: Swedish bank shares jump in merger/results spree.

text.p: Shares in Swedish banks Swedbank and Foreningsbanken jumped on Tuesday when trading resumed after a merger announcement.
Within the first few minutes of trade, Swedbank shares soared 20.5 crowns to 140 crowns after initially opening 15 higher.
Foreningsbanken shares rose five to 43.4 crowns after opening three higher.
"(The merger) was very much expected and everyone was waiting for it," said Paribas analyst Peter Thorn.
Swedish bank shares jump in merger/results=2
The merger between Swedbank and Foreningsbanken was foreshadowed on Monday with a joint statement saying merger talks were underway.
Trading in the shares of both banks was suspended before the Stockholm bourse opened on Monday.
Both banks also posted their 1996 results on Tuesday.
Swedbank's numbers were better-than-expected. The bank posted a 20 percent rise in operating profit to 5.30 billion crowns. Market expectations were for a profit of 4.99 billion crowns.
Foreningsbanken anounced a 14 percent rise in 1996 operating profits to 1.16 billion crowns. Analysts had expected a profit of 1.13 billion crowns.
Activity in the bank sector was hectic on Tuesday with the sector's index surging 5.01 percent by 1410 GMT compared to a general bourse index rise of 0.67 percent.
All the major banks have now reported their 1996 earnings and most came in better than expected, emphasising that the sector has returned to health after the property crisis of the early 1990s.
"I think 1996 was a particularly good season partly due to the sharp decline in interest rates," said Dworsky.
"We will not see the same kind of profit rises now that we have seen in the past few years but restructuring talks will continue."
Handelsbanken reported a 33 percent rise in operating profit in 1996 to 6.72 billion crowns against market expectation of 6.03 billion.
The bank said it had benefited from restructuring its bond portfolio which improved 1996 results by 621 million crowns.
Its shares rose 7.5 crowns to 208.5 crowns.
State-controlled bank Nordbanken reported a 10 percent lift in 1996 operating profit to 7.43 billion crowns. The market expected the bank to prost a profit of 7.29 billion crowns.
Its shares were eight higher in afternoon trade at 243 crowns.
S-E-Banken, which posted a better-than-expected 68 percent leap in 1996 profits last Friday, edged up 1.5 crowns to 76.50 crowns.
Two weeks ago merger talks between S-E-Banken and Nordbanken collapsed.
Analysts said the merger of Swedbank/Foreningsbanken and the merger of Handelsbanken/Stadshypotek that was finalised this week could trigger the other two banks to re-think.
Nordbanken's managing director Hans Dahlborg said on Tuesday that the doors were still open to continue talks with possible future partners.
-- Belinda Goldsmith, Stockholm newsroom +46-8-700 1017
